_meta: A human approval for one irreversible tool call, and a different call sitting in the execution slot by the time the harness runs it, used to show that a confirmation must be bound to the exact call it approved -- the tool name and the full arguments -- not treated as a standing 'yes, proceed'. Gating irreversible tools decides which calls need a human's approval; it does not guarantee that the call the human approved is the call that runs. Between the approval and the execution the pending call can change: the model regenerates the step, a compaction reshuffles state, or -- the dangerous case -- an instruction injected through a tool result rewrites the arguments. If the approval is just a boolean the harness carries forward, it authorizes whatever call is pending at execution time, so a 'yes' meant for deleting a scratch file can end up deleting the quarter's final report. The fix is to bind the approval to a fingerprint of the exact approved call (a hash of its canonical tool+arguments) and, at execution, recompute the fingerprint of the call actually about to run and require it to match -- if the call changed, the old approval does not apply and the harness must gate again. approved_call is the call the human saw and approved; pending_call is what sits in the execution slot when the harness fires (here the path has been changed to a far more destructive target). The two fingerprints, what each harness executes, and whether an unchanged call still passes are computed. Stdlib only.
